subject: english
title: The sentence: subject, action, and meaning
objective: Identify the complete subject and predicate, then explain how a sentence makes its meaning clear.

lesson.opening: A complete sentence makes a claim. The subject names what the sentence is about, and the predicate says what that subject does, is, or experiences.

sections.heading: Find the subject
sections.body: Ask who or what the sentence is about. In “Patient effort removes mountains,” the complete subject is “Patient effort.” The adjective patient belongs with the noun effort.

sections.heading: Find the predicate
sections.body: The predicate includes the verb and the words that complete its meaning. “Removes mountains” tells what patient effort does, so it is the complete predicate.

sections.heading: Repair a fragment
sections.body: A fragment may suggest a scene without making a complete claim. “After the long climb” needs a subject and a predicate: “After the long climb, the hikers rested.”

activities.prompt: In “Patient effort removes mountains,” which words form the complete subject?
activities.hint: Ask who or what the sentence is about.

activities.prompt: Explain what the predicate adds to the subject in the example sentence.
activities.instructions: Write one or two sentences using the words subject and predicate.

activities.prompt: Turn this fragment into a complete sentence: “After the long climb.”
activities.instructions: Add a subject and a predicate while keeping the original idea.
